voice: Rameses remains educated, formal, and anxious while Olympia stays cheerfully morbid; standard spelling replaces the written lisp without changing the Toledo sword, coercive tattoo reveal, or Egyptian sun-symbol clue.

entries.text: Now, Dr. Myklos, what was it you wanted?
I saw you admiring the swords on some of the armor displays, so I thought you might like to see this beautiful specimen of Mr. Heimlich's.
Oh! Thank you, I suppose. It is quite beautiful. Was it forged in Toledo?
Yes, it was. Wol--Mr. Heimlich keeps it very sharp, as you can see. It's--STOP!
Mr. Heimlich has been having trouble with the mounting of that sword, Mr. Najeer. If you touched it, it would probably fall from the wall and kill you.
Good heavens... How can I thank you, Dr. Myklos? You seem to have saved my life.
Let me think. Do you have any scars or tattoos, Mr. Najeer?
Well, yes. I suppose I do. A foolish indulgence from my impulsive youth.
Please let me see it, Mr. Najeer. It would make me very happy.
Dr. Myklos, this is rather embarrassing. I would prefer not to.
Are you forgetting that I just saved you from almost certain beheading?
*Sigh* Very well. I will show you. One moment, please, while I remove my shoes.
There. But look quickly. What if someone comes in?
How beautiful! Egyptian sun symbols, yes?
Yes. May I put my shoes back on now, please?
Oh, if you must. I've never seen tattoos on the soles of someone's feet before. Did it hurt very much? Did you bleed?
